materials.activation: data-material="glass"; data-appearance chooses light or dark.
materials.blurMapping: CSS blur sigma is half the Figma radius.
materials.readability: Glass supporting text uses glass-text-secondary; fields, media, statuses and approval controls keep readable opaque working surfaces. Shared blue selection stays unchanged.
materials.fallback: Reduced transparency replaces chrome/content/button fills with sidebar/surface/surface-raised and sets blur to 0px. Unsupported backdrop-filter uses the same opaque fills.

appearance.persistence: Allowlisted device-local produdash.appearance local storage, restored before CSS; no workspace, credential or IPC changes. Invalid values fall back to System; unavailable storage retains session selection.
appearance.resolution: System follows OS changes with solid material. Explicit choices override OS; glass choices use the named light/dark appearance.
appearance.switching: Updates root attributes without rerendering content; preserves drafts, focus and playback.

mediaLibrary.selection: Native tile buttons expose aria-pressed, blue selection, actual indexed thumbnail, duration and visible source status.
mediaLibrary.fallback: Existing format placeholder when no indexed thumbnail exists.

timeline.layout: Full editor width beneath preview and inspector; fixed-height SVG inside horizontal scrolling.
timeline.semantics: Edited-time ruler and real cut/source ranges; repeated source thumbnails are illustrative, not per-cut frames. Prepared waveform is labeled Source waveform.
timeline.accessibility: Keyboard-operable cuts, focus stroke, aria-pressed and an accessible cut list.

propertyGroups.layout: Heading and ruled label/control rows; columns prefer 300px and wrap within available width.
propertyGroups.contracts: Keep native form names, constraints, values, disabled states and consent disclosures.

commerce.tables: Read-only scoped headers, tabular numbers, right-aligned amounts and local overflow.
commerce.charts: Independent caller-supplied series; zero, negative and unavailable values retained. More than eight periods scroll horizontally.
commerce.exactData: Dashboard screen-reader table; Analytics visible period/revenue table.
commerce.authority: Existing theme tokens; no new palette or static assets.

uiPatterns.verification: See docs/ui-expansion.md. Full validation passed (486 unit tests, four Electron smoke tests); a decoded-frame recapture also passed. Final visual review marked SHIP for the captured matrix (124 current images). The app was opened.

narrative.overview:
ProduDash uses a compact, calm working interface adapted from the owner’s shared macOS Figma kit. Solid surfaces, restrained borders and a single blue selection language connect commerce operations, conversations and the media editor. This name describes the implemented direction; it does not introduce a new visual concept.

System-following solid light and dark appearances carry the same hierarchy. The approved optional Glass Light and Glass Dark variants extend this system with translucent materials from the kit’s Native Fidelity Lab; the solid themes remain available. Local system typography and bundled artwork keep the interface self-contained. Native window chrome, readable status text and explicit approval controls remain part of the working surface.
keyCharacteristics: Solid defaults and optional glass surfaces with shared blue selection.
Reserved space for Juanito and real editing controls.

rules.name: The Shared Blue Rule
rules.body: Use the shared blue family for selection and primary actions across all sections; preserve semantic status colors with visible text.

rules.name: The Local Type Rule
rules.body: Use the existing local system font stack; introduce no runtime font service.

rules.name: The Reserved Space Rule
rules.body: Place Juanito in the workspace grid and his launcher in the sidebar footer so neither covers approval or timeline controls.

rules.name: The Optional Material Rule
rules.body: Keep System solid by default. Apply chrome, content and button glass recipes only for explicit glass choices, retaining readable opaque working surfaces and reduced-transparency fallbacks.

dos: Do default to System, honor explicit appearance choices and preserve the shared blue hierarchy.
Do use the scoped chrome/content/button recipes for glass and opaque fallback surfaces when transparency is reduced or blur unavailable.
Do keep keyboard focus visible, tab selection semantic, and state labels readable.
Do reflow panels at narrow effective widths and keep timeline scrolling inside its own container.
Do preserve native window controls, bundled Juanito artwork and local system typography.
donts: Don't substitute family-specific yellow or red accents for shared blue selection.
Don't add whole-window horizontal overflow or overlay Juanito on working controls.
Don't remove status text, approval boundaries, consent disclosures or unavailable states to simplify a layout.
Don't introduce remote runtime font or media dependencies.
